title: Regional coordination: circuit-breaker, election and DR playbook (WIP)
content:
Purpose / quick summary:
This is a working sketch for how regional control planes coordinate routing, leader election, and disaster recovery for Redwood’s inference fabric. The goal is to define practical, operator-friendly modes that balance strong safety (no split-brain), fast recovery, and predictable request steering for latency-sensitive customers (hosted API + Dedicated).

Context and constraints (short):
- We run control-plane instances in N regions (typically 3 primary regions + standby regions).
- Customer-facing routing decisions must: prefer region-local serving (latency), respect isolation (Dedicated), and fall back gracefully during regional degradation.
- We must avoid split-brain on mutable control-plane state (rollouts, reserved capacity leases, topology ownership).
- Operators value deterministic failover and a short, auditable DR playbook.

High-level options considered (and quick trade-offs):
1) Active-active with optimistic routing + lease-based soft leaders
   - Runtime: All regions accept reads/most writes; each mutating operation acquires a short, per-namespace lease (50–300ms) from a local arbiter.
   - Pros: low-latency reads, no single-point leader, incremental degradations possible.
   - Cons: higher complexity to avoid conflicting mutates; requires robust fast reconciliation and monotonic epochs to detect stale writes.

2) Active-passive with explicit primary leases and manual/automated promotion
   - Runtime: One region is the authoritative primary for a given tenancy/cluster; secondaries are read-only and receive async updates. Promotion happens on explicit operator action or automated health checks plus safety gating.
   - Pros: simpler correctness model, easier audit of mutations, deterministic ownership for billing/allocations.
   - Cons: higher latency for non-primary clients and potentially slower failover.

3) Hybrid: soft-primary + local-fast-path + conflict-resolution on commit
   - Runtime: Each region has a notion of preferred-primary per shard; operations attempt local fast-path then reconcile at commit time using causal metadata (epochs + op ids).
   - Pros: compromise between latency and safety; limits cross-region chatter to commit windows.
   - Cons: complexity in conflict resolution and potential transient divergence.

Routing policy patterns (operator-facing):
- Region-preferred, tier-aware steering: prefer local region for hosted and racked Dedicated where allowed; fall back candidate list ordered by (latency, tier-match, capacity score).
- Circuit-breaker for region degradation: if region health < threshold or error-rate spike occurs, mark region as TRIPPED for Xs and divert a fraction of new requests to next candidate. Use exponential backoff with operator override.
- Sticky allocations for stateful sessions: when a request opens a long-lived session (websocket, streaming), pin to region unless circuit-breaker trips; provide auto-handoff hooks to drain and re-establish session in new region.

Leader election models evaluated:
A) Paxos/Raft-style strong consensus for control-plane membership (full quorum)
   - Use when we need strong linearizability for certain resources (billing ledger, reserved capacity commits).
   - Quorum costs cross-region latency; we can restrict to regional quorums per tenancy to reduce p99.

B) Lease-token arbitration (lease manager per namespace)
   - Lightweight: lease tokens issued with TTLs; renewals can be batched. Detect broken leases with clock skew tolerance.
   - Good for short-lived leadership and fast failover; weaker if clock discontinuities occur.

C) Epidemic-style epoch propagation + monotonic stamps
   - Writes tagged with epoch/counter and reconciled after-the-fact. Useful when most operations are commutative or idempotent.

Recommendation (middle path, staged rollout):
- Adopt a hybrid model: use consensus (Raft) for a small set of global-critical resources (account metadata, billing commitments) where strict correctness is mandatory.
- Use lease-based soft-leaders for per-tenant routing metadata, model pinning, and capacity leases (short TTLs, renewable).
- Implement a local fast-path for reads and optimistic writes that can succeed under soft-leader, but require a commit handshake to upgrade to durable state.

DR / failover playbook (operator steps - automated where possible):
1) Detection: automatic healthscoring evaluates CPU/GPU saturation, API error rates, underlying network partitions, and control-plane leader liveness.
2) Soft-failover (automated): trigger circuit-breaker; send traffic fractionally to next candidate (10% -> 50% -> 100%) while starting a reconcile job to ensure metadata is consistent in target region.
3) Promote (semi-auto): if promote-safety checks pass (no lease-holder heartbeat, reconciled state ok, safety-latches clear), auto-promote soft-leader in target region. Notify ops channel and create audit event.
4) Hard-failover (manual): if auto-promote fails or data inconsistency suspected, ops run manual promotion checklist (see checklist below).
5) Recovery: when the original region becomes healthy, we prefer a safe rejoin flow: do not auto-demote new primary; instead run a controlled backfill and operator-acknowledge handback.

Operator checklist for manual promotion (playbook):
- Confirm region health metrics and estimate ETA to recover.
- Verify last committed epoch/sequence for tenancy shards.
- Run reconciliation dry-run and preview diffs.
- Acquire manual 'promotion lock' (one-time gate) in central audit log.
- Execute promote + soft traffic cutover (10% -> 100%), observe error-rate and latency for 5m.
- If any unexpected divergence, roll back traffic and re-open investigation.

Design specifics and safety knobs:
- Monotonic epoch stamped on all mutates; append-only log for critical arenas (billing, reserved capacity).
- Dual-write guard: optimistic local write + background cross-region commit with compensating actions on conflict.
- Circuit-breaker hysteresis: min-trip-duration = 30s, initial backoff = 10s, multiplier = 2, max backoff = 10m. Manual override always possible from Console.
- Observability: per-tenant, per-region timelines for leases, commit epochs, and reconciliation status. Alerts on reordering or gap in epoch sequence.

Open questions and things to validate in POC:
- Lease TTL tuning: how short can TTL be before renew churn dominates under high tenancy scale?
- Clock skew behavior: how do we harden lease/epoch detection if customer infra has large skew induced by live migration?
- Failure injection: need to run cross-region partition drills to validate circuit-breaker hysteresis + eventual consistency reconcilers.
- Billing correctness when traffic is split across primaries temporarily (race between commit and billing ledger).

Action items / next steps (short list):
- POC: implement soft-leader + epoch markers for single-tenant shard and run chaos tests (owner: Liam, due 2026-04-10).
- Run 3 failure-drills in staging that simulate region partition + partial partition + noisy neighbor (owner: Priya, due 2026-04-30).
- Draft Console operator UI for promotion override and traffic-steering with audit trail (owner: UX squad, Noah to coordinate).
- Write a concise DR playbook doc targeted at SRE on-call rotation (owner: Maya).

Appendix: quick ascii sketches
1) Active-passive promotion timeline:
   region-a(primary) --(heartbeat)-> region-b(secondary)
   partition occurs -> region-b detects missing heartbeat -> operator proms
2) Circuit-breaker steering heuristic (pseudocode):
   if error_rate(region) > err_thresh or latency_p95(region) > p95_thresh:
     trip(region)
     divert_fraction = compute_diversion_score(region_health)
     backoff_timer.start(region)

Notes-to-self: keep wording in our public runbook conservative; avoid promising fully automated promotions until POC stability is proven.

References / links:
- Confluence: Multiregion Control Plane Index (see linked_artifacts)
- Jira: PLAT-4821 (multiregion reconciliation work)
- PR: platform/pull/2345 - initial soft-leader implementation

Unresolved debates to surface in next sync:
- Strong consensus vs lightweight leases per-tenant: cost of quorum vs simplicity of leases.
- Whether to allow brief dual-write windows for faster failover (optimize for p99) vs strictly serialized commit model.

End of working sketch.

(If you're reading and have specific tests to add, drop them inline below — this doc is intentionally informal.)
